name: EU AI Act
description: EU AI Act overlay for AI systems operating in or serving the EU market. First regulation directly governing AI agent behavior. Applies comprehensive requirements for high-risk AI systems including risk management, data governance, transparency, human oversight, and accuracy. Trigger updated in v0.3 to include DC-GEN (general-purpose AI outputs and model-generated content): any EU-serving agent producing general-purpose AI outputs is subject to the GPAI provisions of the EU AI Act regardless of specific data classification.

evidence_requirements: Risk management system established and maintained throughout AI system lifecycle (Art.9.1)
Quality management system ensuring compliance with AI Act requirements (Art.17)
Deployer obligations documented — monitoring, human oversight, and reporting responsibilities assigned (Art.26)
Provider and deployer responsibilities clearly delineated
Risk management system identifies and analyzes known and foreseeable risks (Art.9.2)
Residual risks communicated to deployers with appropriate mitigation measures (Art.9.3)
Human oversight measures enabling overseers to understand AI system capacities and limitations (Art.14.4a)
Capability for human overseer to interpret AI system output (Art.14.4b)
Ability to decide not to use, override, or reverse AI system output (Art.14.4d, Art.14.4e)
Ability to intervene in or halt AI system operation (Art.14.4f)

threshold_adjustments.reason: Art.14 mandates human oversight for high-risk AI systems — human overseers must be able to understand, interpret, and override

evidence_requirements: AI system registered in EU database before placing on market or putting into service (Art.49)
Registration includes system description, intended purpose, and provider information
Components and third-party elements documented in technical documentation (Art.11)
Third-party pre-trained models and data sources identified
Training, validation, and testing datasets documented with data governance measures (Art.10)
Data quality criteria defined and verified (Art.10.2)
Bias examination and mitigation measures documented (Art.10.2f)
Third-party components and their impact on AI system documented
Supply chain transparency for AI model providers
Risk assessment identifying known and foreseeable risks of AI system (Art.9.2)
Risk classification determination documented (Art.6, Art.7)
Note: Risk classification is an operator determination — Ancilis provides evidence but cannot classify risk level for the operator
AI system identifiable as AI to persons interacting with it (Art.50 transparency)
Provider identity and contact information available

threshold_adjustments.reason: Art.50 requires AI system to be identifiable as AI to users

evidence_requirements: AI system operates within intended purpose boundaries (Art.9.4)
Measures to prevent misuse outside intended purpose documented
AI system designed to achieve appropriate levels of accuracy, robustness, and cybersecurity (Art.15)
Technical redundancy and fail-safe measures documented
Data governance measures implemented for training and operational data (Art.10)
Data protection by design and by default applied
Automatic logging of AI system events throughout lifecycle (Art.12.1)
Logs enable traceability of AI system operation at each stage (Art.12.2)
Log retention for duration set by implementing member state or sector-specific rules (Art.12.3)

threshold_adjustments.reason: Art.12 requires automatic logging with traceability throughout lifecycle

evidence_requirements: System configurations documented in technical documentation (Annex IV)
Configuration changes tracked and validated
Appropriate cybersecurity measures against unauthorized access and data poisoning (Art.15.4)
Security measures proportionate to risk level
AI system resilient against errors, faults, and attempts to alter output by unauthorized third parties (Art.15.3)
Robustness measures including technical redundancy (Art.15.4)
Post-market monitoring system tracks AI system performance over lifetime (Art.72)
Monitoring includes detection of potential biases, accuracy degradation, and safety issues (Art.9.2)
Anomaly detection for deviation from expected behavior

threshold_adjustments.reason: Art.9.2 and Art.72 require ongoing risk monitoring and post-market surveillance

evidence_requirements: Configuration monitoring ensures system operates as documented in technical documentation
Changes to AI system detected and validated against approved configurations
Conformity assessment completed before placing AI system on market (Art.43)
Post-market monitoring data analyzed for compliance trends (Art.72)
Log integrity verified — automatic logging records not tampered with (Art.12)
Traceability of AI system operation maintained
Corrective actions taken when AI system presents risks (Art.16g)
Non-compliant AI systems withdrawn or recalled (Art.16g)
Human oversight allows intervention in or halt of AI system operation (Art.14.4f)
Escalation paths to market surveillance authorities defined for serious incidents
Serious incident evidence preserved and reported to market surveillance authorities (Art.73)
Technical documentation available for inspection (Art.18)
Corrective actions and recovery procedures documented (Art.16g)
System can be withdrawn or recalled when presenting risks
Post-market monitoring feeds back into risk management system (Art.9, Art.72)
Lessons learned incorporated into system improvements

reporting_obligations.assessment_type: Conformity assessment for high-risk AI systems (Art.43). Self-assessment or third-party assessment depending on AI system category. CE marking required. Registration in EU AI database mandatory (Art.49).
reporting_obligations.reporting_entity: Market surveillance authority of the relevant EU member state. Serious incidents reported per Art.73. Providers must cooperate with competent national authorities.

human_oversight_mandates.description: Art.14 mandates human oversight for high-risk AI systems. Human overseers must be able to: understand the AI system's capacities and limitations (14.4a), remain aware of automation bias (14.4b), correctly interpret output (14.4c), decide not to use or override output (14.4d-e), and intervene in or halt operation (14.4f).

PR-01.regulatory_citation: EU AI Act Art.16, Art.50 — Provider obligations and transparency

PR-05.regulatory_citation: EU AI Act Art.12 — Automatic record-keeping

DE-01.regulatory_citation: EU AI Act Art.9.2, Art.72 — Risk management and post-market monitoring

GOV-04.regulatory_citation: EU AI Act Art.14 — Human oversight for high-risk AI systems

notes: EU AI Act is the first regulation directly governing AI agent behavior. Enforcement phases: prohibited AI practices (Feb 2025), GPAI model obligations (Aug 2025), high-risk AI system obligations (Aug 2026). This overlay enforces strict monitoring, logging, and human oversight. Risk classification is an operator determination — Ancilis provides the evidence package but cannot classify risk level for the operator.
